name: App Store / static image-pack creatives
summary: Golden set for a pack of static app-store-style / performance creatives: real-surface grounding, legible value prop, and a true scroll-stop frame vs. the generic-stock, hallucinated-UI, and palette-drift failures.

examples.label: good
features: Hero frame shows the ACTUAL product UI/screenshot grounded from a site crawl, not a generic stock dashboard
One value prop per creative, legible at thumbnail scale (large weight, high contrast, safe margins)
Palette matches the real brand tokens (computed CSS hex), not an invented neon scheme
Set covers distinct angles across creatives (proof, feature, social) so the matrix is testable, not 1 idea x N
Any product claim is grounded in real copy/features, no invented SDK or fabricated metric
examples.notes: Site-grounded, single-message, brand-true. This is the bar the fb-creatives skill + AGENTS #15 site-grounding enforce.

examples.label: acceptable
features: Brand palette correct and value prop legible, but the hero leans on a clean mockup rather than a real screenshot
Message is single and clear but the angle overlaps another creative in the pack (limited variation)
Type hierarchy readable but slightly tight in the safe zone
examples.notes: Ships, but flag the weak variation + mockup-over-real-surface for the next pass.

examples.label: bad
features: Generic stock dashboard / invented UI that does not match the real product surface
Wrong palette (e.g. magenta-cyan neon) drifting from the brand's actual tokens
Multiple competing messages crammed into one frame, none legible at thumbnail scale
Hallucinated proof: a fake `import <brand>` SDK snippet or an unverified metric the brand never claims
Tiny low-contrast text that disappears at feed scale
examples.notes: Caught on sotaocr-fb-001: a $1.20 wrong-palette burn + 5/32 creatives with a hallucinated Python SDK. Both preventable by site-grounding (AGENTS #15) + verifying the SDK before code-creative.
